Course 21

Parenting and family

Attachment, parenting styles, limits and emotions in the family, with what research says and no magic recipes.

Lesson 3. Emotions and limits

1 · Lesson

Young children cannot regulate their emotions on their own: they learn with adults' help, first through their presence and calm (co-regulation) and gradually by putting words to what they feel. Tantrums between the ages of two and four are a normal part of development.

John Gottman described the "emotion coach" style: adults who see a child's emotions as a chance to connect, name them, validate them and, when needed, set limits on behaviour. Validating an emotion does not mean allowing any behaviour: "I understand you're angry, but we don't hit".

Limits give security when they are few, clear, consistent and age-appropriate. Consequences related to the behaviour and announced in advance work better than impulsive punishments. And adults' example teaches more than lectures.

2 · Example

A three-year-old throws a toy because a piece will not fit. Instead of "it's not a big deal", the adult can say: "it's frustrating that it won't go in, isn't it? Let's take a breath and try together". Naming the emotion helps calm it and teaches emotional vocabulary.

3 · Activity

Write down three rules you consider important at home or in a group you know. For each, check whether it is clear, whether the reason for it is explained and whether it has a known consequence.
